correctness.rationale: Reconstructs the exact parity rule for all independent edge families and checks the distinct 2-edge, proper-star, full-star, triangle, and singleton cases. At most one full star, so optimizing colors reduces exactly to a maximum edge-disjoint triangle packing on K_n or K_(n-1); Schönheim leave sizes give all six residues and the n=6 tie. The C++ exhaustive exact colored partition DP n=5,6,7 and a separate MILP-based construction plus direct parity verification n=5..10 agree; finite checks do not substitute for the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The initial 2024 strong-odd papers introduce and bound the invariant without computing the infinite rank-two Kneser family. The 2025 general Kneser odd-independence theorem only specifies maximum single-class sizes and its Petersen proposition gives the previously known n=5 value. The classical maximum triangle-packing theorem supplies the packing leaves, but not the parity-based classification of all coloring classes or the forced-star transition. Relevant published research-record hits do not imply the new full formula. Priority risk from unindexed work is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Historical priority may be affected by unindexed or unpublished conversions of maximum partial triple systems into strong-odd colorings.
The original 1966 paper was not directly obtained; an accessible detailed construction-based university exposition supplies its stated maximum-packing theorem.
The 2025 Petersen instance is preexisting and is excluded from the claim of genuinely new rank-two family results.
No external independent audit of the new proof has been performed.

value.rationale: A complete infinite-family graph-coloring invariant and all optimal color partition structures are obtained. The parity-induced transition from triangle-only partitions at odd orders to a forced full-star color at even n>=8, with n=6 tied families, is structurally meaningful and connects graph coloring to partial Steiner triple systems; no arbitrary finite cutoff or mere published table recalculation.
